label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Inês: launch Thursday 26 November

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family in the Netherlands. I left tonight and I don't know yet for how long, so Thursday is yours.

I am sorry. Handing you a launch three days before is bad enough, and I only found the error in figure 3 this afternoon, so you get it with a hole in it.

Two things before the list.

The 2.1 is my mistake, not yours. If anyone asks how it happened, say so, with my name.

And I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do, and annex B is your work. I have not forgotten Lisbon, where the projector died and you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think.

WHAT IS WRONG

Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, without the free allocation phase-out applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does.

- Corrected: PDF v7 on the drive (pages 3, 14 and 15).
- Not corrected: deck v4 (slides 6 and 9).
- Not corrected: the embargoed press release, which says 2.1. Hanna sent it on Friday to 34 Brussels contacts.

The embargo lifts Thursday at 10:00. My note with the details is in this folder ("ERROR figure 3").

TUESDAY, IN THIS ORDER

1. Hanna and the press release. This comes first, because every hour it waits a journalist may be drafting with 2.1.
- Assume she knows nothing yet. Tell her about the error, give her 1.4 and point her to v7.
- A corrected release should go to the same 34 contacts, clearly marked as a correction, with the same embargo.
- If she wants a senior name on it, Geert can sign off. He knows I am away. Give him the two-line version of the error when you ask.
- From now on only v7 goes out, gets linked or gets printed.

2. Tomás in Lindqvist's office (tomas.reyes@ep-office-lindqvist.example). He wrote this morning and I have not answered.
- The MEP has a vote and must leave at 13:30.
- He asks for a presentation of 15 minutes instead of 20, with the panel starting at 12:50.
- She wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes.

Please tell him:
- You are presenting and sitting on the panel in my place.
- Yes to the new timings.
- The headline figure is now 1.4, in case her welcome or briefing uses the old one.

And ask him who moderates after 13:30, and whether the Q&A still runs to 14:00. He did not say.

3. The deck.
- Change slides 6 and 9 to 1.4 and redo the chart on 9.
- Check the speaker notes for the old number too.
- Cut it to 15 minutes. You know better than I do what can go.
- The notes are mine, written for me. Make it your talk.

I would put the correction in the presentation yourself, in one sentence, early: an earlier version said 2.1, the right figure is 1.4, the conclusion stands. Then nobody else gets to announce it.

WEDNESDAY

4. Before 12:00, final names to Tomás for the badges.
- After 12:00, security will not let people in.
- Take me off, and make sure you are on it, plus anyone else coming from our side.
- Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is coming with a colleague. Check that both are covered and get the colleague's name.

5. Press calls at 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each.
- One is a trade newsletter and one a Belgian daily.
- They asked for background before the event and Hanna told them I would be available.
- Hanna still has to confirm the slots and tell them it will be you.
- Both have the 2.1 release, so the correction must reach them before you speak, and I would open each call with it.

THURSDAY

- 10:00: the embargo lifts.
- 12:00: guests at the security entrance of the Altiero Spinelli building. Tomás collects the badges. There is a light lunch outside the room.
- 12:30: welcome by Lindqvist (5 minutes).
- 12:35: your presentation (15 minutes).
- 12:50: panel with Abena Owusu-Mensah (remote), Florian Kessler and you. Lindqvist moderates until she leaves at 13:30.
- The old run of show has Q&A at 13:40 and close at 14:00. What happens after 13:30 depends on what Tomás answers.

Abena should hear from you before Thursday that it is you on the panel and that the figure changed.

KESSLER

He will try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through. His comments of 12 November are in the folder, and so are my reply lines. Do not let him set the tone.
- 80% is the central case.
- Your annex B runs 40% and 60%.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.

Say that openly and without getting defensive. Nobody in that room knows those runs as you do.

On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. It is in section 5.2 and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.

If he uses the correction to put the rest in doubt, the answer is short. One figure came from an old run, it is fixed, and the conclusion is the same.

Abena was strong on the call and will probably back us on the LDC side. Bring her in.

AFTERWARDS

Lucy Tran needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers for their grant report, ideally by 4 December. Ask someone to take photos during the panel and to count the room, because you will not have a hand free. In her email she congratulated both of us on getting the paper finished, by name.

REACHING ME

You can call me, tonight on the train or tomorrow morning. From 9 tomorrow I may not pick up, so leave a message.

You do not need my permission for anything on this list. If you have to decide something and cannot reach me, decide it, and I will stand behind it.

Marieke
